Subject: SunPrep: FERPA & GLBA addenda request — next steps

Team,

Quick summary: Sunrise Prep (K-12 district) surfaced a request for a FERPA addendum and wants to confirm our subprocessor commitments for student data. Separately, Northshore Bank (pilot) raised GLBA questions during procurement and asked if we can map data flows and provide a GLBA clause set. Both asks impact our DPA templates and subprocessor disclosure cadence.

Immediate asks:
- Stephanie: can Legal reuse the HIPAA/BAA playbook as a template or do we need new language for FERPA/GLBA?
- Ben: can you produce a short subprocessor export (last 90 days) plus the proposed residency/transfer guarantees we can offer for US K-12?
- Grace: timeline on SOC/Audit artifacts we can share (redaction guidance).

Attachments: I pulled the initial redline from SunPrep (SunPrep_DPA_redline_v1.docx). They also attached a FERPA checklist we should review.

Goal: respond to Sunrise with a clear feasibility note + proposed timeline by EOD Tuesday. If any procurement/legal blockers, flag them now so I can escalate to Sarah (CRO).

Thanks,
Alex
--
Alex Martinez
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SunPrep: FERPA & GLBA addenda request — next steps

Thanks for the summary. High level: we can reuse large parts of the HIPAA/BAA framework (data classification, access controls, encryption-in-transit/at-rest) but FERPA has student-education-record-specific definitions and parental rights language we must incorporate. GLBA needs explicit consumer financial data definitions and a different data-share consent model.

Action items I propose:
1) I will draft two short addendum templates (FERPA addendum, GLBA addendum) and annotate where language differs from our standard DPA. Target: Tue 4/14 EOD.
2) Ben, please attach the subprocessor export and the residency guarantees (e.g., US-only cache TTL, cancelable export) — we need to confirm whether any subprocessors process unencrypted content.
3) Grace, please locate the most recent SOC-2 report and the document retention policy we can share redacted.

We should loop Legal for the FERPA parental-rights phrasing; I suggest Maya Chen (external counsel) as she's done K-12 DPAs before. I'll forward the redline to her with comments.

-Steph
--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@sunrise-prep.org>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sunrise-prep.org
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FERPA & GLBA addenda implementation pathways

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up. A few clarifications from our end before you draft:

- FERPA scope: we only need the addendum to cover PII in education records for K-12 students when Redwood processes student-submitted content and grading metadata.
- Subprocessors: we must publish a list and get 30-day notice for additions. We understand sensitive infra vendors may be redacted but need a contact for escalation.
- Data residency: Sunrise requires that student content for our district be stored within US regions; ephemeral caching in other regions is permitted for inference if TTL < 1 hour.

Attachments: Our procurement team attached a short checklist (FERPA_QA_checklist.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood's current subprocessor list includes a third-party logging provider that ingests unencrypted logs? That is a hard blocker for our board.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director of IT & Data Privacy
Sunrise Preparatory School District
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SunPrep: FERPA & GLBA addenda implementation pathways

Alex / Steph — attaching the quick export: GLBA_party_matrix.xlsx shows subprocessors with processing roles and whether they see plaintext. Summary: no logging provider receives unencrypted student content; logs are pseudonymized and access-controlled. We do use a third-party telemetry pipeline (TelemetryCo) that receives metadata (error traces, token counts) but no student PII, and it's configurable to drop payloads for specific customers.

I also confirmed our storage for K-12 customers can be pinned to US regions; inference edges may run in multi-region pools but we can add TTL constraints (suggest 30m default for student content).

Attachments: GLBA_party_matrix.xlsx

—Ben
Ben Carter

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed next steps and timeline (Sunrise Prep FERPA addendum)

Alicia — thanks for the clarifications and for the checklist. Quick update and next steps: 

1) Feasibility: Redwood can support the FERPA scope you described. We can commit to US-only storage for student content and configurable inference TTLs. We will provide a subprocessor list and 30-day notice for changes; for sensitive subprocessors we will provide a redacted entry plus a named escalation contact.

2) Attachments & artifacts: Stephanie (Legal) will draft a FERPA addendum and annotate points that differ from our standard DPA. Ben attached an operations matrix confirming no subprocessor ingests unencrypted student content (see GLBA_party_matrix.xlsx). Grace will provide a redacted SOC-2 and retention policy.

3) Timeline:
- Tue 4/14: Legal draft (FERPA addendum v0.1) and internal review.
- Thu 4/16: Redwood to send draft + artifacts (SOC-2 redacted, subprocessor matrix) to Sunrise procurement.
- Week of 4/20: Contract negotiation / redlines.

If Sunrise's board requires a stricter TTL than 30 minutes or an explicit on-prem option, flag that as a potential procurement escalation and we will discuss Dedicated/Private deployment pricing.

Next step for Sunrise — please confirm the TTL cap (30m is proposed) and whether you need an on-site / air-gapped deployment option documented now.

Regards,
Alex
